definition: A method that estimates distribution parameters as the values that maximize the likelihood of the observed data.
comment: It is the most widely used method for Weibull parameters; it is solved iteratively and is efficient for large samples.

definition: A variant of the maximum likelihood method that estimates distribution parameters from wind speeds grouped in frequency classes.
comment: It is used when wind data are available as a frequency distribution rather than as a time series.

definition: A method that estimates distribution parameters by equating sample moments, such as the mean and variance, to the theoretical moments.
comment: It is simple to apply and often gives Weibull parameters close to those of maximum likelihood.

definition: A method that estimates parameters by minimizing the sum of squared differences between observed and fitted values.
comment: For the Weibull distribution it fits a straight line to the linearized cumulative distribution.

definition: A method that estimates distribution parameters from a straight-line fit on probability paper or a linearized plot.
comment: For the Weibull distribution, the slope and intercept of ln(−ln(1−F)) versus ln(v) give the shape and scale parameters.

definition: A method that estimates Weibull parameters from the energy pattern factor, the ratio of the mean of the cubed wind speed to the cube of the mean wind speed.
comment: It is quick to apply and preserves the mean wind power density of the data.

definition: A method that estimates Weibull parameters from the mean and the standard deviation of wind speed through an empirical relation.
comment: It is also known as the empirical method; the shape parameter is approximated by (σ/v̄)^−1.086.

definition: An empirical method, proposed by Justus, that estimates the Weibull shape parameter from the ratio of standard deviation to mean wind speed.
comment: It is a common variant of the standard deviation method in wind resource assessment.

definition: A method that estimates Weibull parameters so that the fitted distribution reproduces the observed mean wind speed and mean power density.
comment: It is closely related to the energy pattern factor method.
